piece_type: Instagram post (reel + caption) on company and brand accounts

cases.heading: (none; body text)
cases.claim: “I’m excited about getting rid of my lines…I’m ready to, like, not have them so much.” | “I feel really good. I’m really surprised at how quickly it’s kicking in! And I’m feeling like the line between my eyebrows is gone.” | “*About 50% of patients begin showing improvement after two days. Most patients (~69%) achieve complete results by day 30.”
cases.context: Patient testimonial reel with Day 0/Day 2/Day 30 before-and-after clips; full indication shown only at close of testimonial or by scrolling caption; SUPER 'Individual results may vary' does not mitigate.
cases.rationale: Indication is temporary improvement in glabellar lines; GLS score of 0 ('none') was exploratory with no alpha, so claims that lines are 'gone' or results 'complete' are unsupported.
cases.check: Does the piece imply complete/permanent elimination of the condition when the label supports only temporary or partial improvement?

cases.cat: Misleading presentation of study data (post hoc / exploratory)
cases.heading: (none; body text)
cases.claim: “Lines today. Blurred in as little as 2 days.*…Nope. You’re not seeing things. Jeuveau® really does work like that.” | “With our iconic fast-acting results…”
cases.context: Day 2 data were an exploratory endpoint (>=1-point GLS change, single assessor) intermingled with primary Day 30 composite >=2-point endpoint. OPDP advisory comments (Nov 22, 2019) previously warned about onset claims.
cases.rationale: Onset claims rest on exploratory Day 2 endpoint without multiplicity adjustment and a less stringent response definition; mixing it with the primary endpoint misleads on onset and magnitude.
cases.check: Are speed-of-onset claims ('fast-acting', 'as little as X days') based on a primary/prespecified endpoint, and are differing endpoint definitions kept distinct?

cases.heading: (none; body text)
cases.claim: “…it’s no wonder Jeuveau is making moves to Studio @IPSY for our Blur The Lines Masterclass. Because in 2026, we’re blurring the lines between what’s found in your beauty bag and what happens in the treatment room. [syringe icon] [lipstick icon]”
cases.context: Lively testimonial with upbeat music, fashion/beauty styling; product carries boxed warning for distant spread of toxin effect.
cases.rationale: Likens a prescription injectable with a boxed warning to an everyday cosmetic, oversimplifying dosing/administration requirements and minimizing risk.
cases.check: Does the piece equate a prescription drug with a cosmetic/consumer product or routine in a way that trivializes administration requirements or risks?

cases.cat: Lack of fair balance (risk presentation prominence)
cases.heading: (none; body text)
cases.claim: Risk information presented only at the end of the reel, after the tag line “Jeuveau, you see me” appears for about four seconds against a black background; unnarrated, fast scrolling risk information follows a directive to “ask your doctor if Jeuveau is right for you.”
cases.context: No signal alerts viewers that risk info follows the 38-second testimonial; caption risk info only reachable by scrolling past additional benefit claims.
cases.rationale: Risk information lacks prominence and readability reasonably comparable to benefit presentation, minimizing risks.
cases.check: Rule: in video/social pieces, flag if risk information appears only after a closing tag/end card, is unnarrated or fast-scrolling, or requires scrolling past benefit claims.
